sections.h2: Where is Waterbury, and why is it called the Brass City?
sections.html:
Waterbury is a city in New Haven County, 33 miles southwest of Hartford and 77 miles northeast of New York City. The 2020 census counted 114,403 residents, and a 2024 estimate puts the number at 115,908.

The city covers about 28.95 square miles and sits along the Naugatuck River valley, with Interstate 84 and Route 8 meeting downtown. It is the largest city in the Naugatuck Valley Planning Region and the second largest in New Haven County.

The Brass City nickname comes from the 19th and early 20th century, when Waterbury was a leading American center for brass manufacturing. It also produced clocks and watches, including Robert Ingersoll's one dollar pocket watch, and silverware. The city's motto, Quid Aere Perennius, translates as "What Is More Lasting Than Brass?" Many of those old factories and clock towers are still landmarks.

sections.h2: How old are Waterbury's houses, and what does that mean at tax time?
sections.html:
The 2022 revaluation notice from the city explains that residential values grew much faster than commercial values, so many homeowners saw higher bills even though the mill rate fell.

Waterbury has 25 recognized neighborhoods, including these.

  • Brooklyn, Bunker Hill, Hillside and the East End
  • Overlook, Town Plot, Washington Hill and Fairmount
  • Hopeville, Waterville, Pine Hill and Long Hill
  • Country Club, Crownbrook, Robinwood and Bucks Hill
  • North End, South End, West Side and WOW (Walnut-Orange-Walsh)

Town Plot is where the original 1674 settlement stood, before King Philip's War forced people out and the community moved east along the Mad River in 1677. Neighborhood affects value, and the assessor's records will show how your parcel is valued compared with its neighbors.

sections.h2: How did the 2022 revaluation work in Waterbury?
sections.html:
Waterbury completed a state-mandated five-year revaluation for the October 1, 2022 Grand List, and the new values were used for the 2023 to 2024 budget year that began July 1, 2023. The city had a choice between full implementation and a phase-in of up to five years.

The city's own notice compared the two options with projected mill rates. A full implementation was estimated at about 40 mills. A five-year phase-in used a proposed rate of 55.50 mills. Those were planning estimates published before the budget vote, not the rate on your bill, so check the Tax Collector for the figure actually adopted.

The notice also says a phase-in applies only to increases. Any decreases in assessed value are not phased in, and the Board of Aldermen can end a phase-in early.

OptionEstimated mill rate in the 2022 noticeEffect on most residential owners
Full implementationAbout 40 millsLarger immediate bill
Five-year phase-in55.50 mills proposedIncrease spread over up to five years

sections.h2: What does the Waterbury Assessor's Office do?
sections.html:
The Assessor's Office appraises property at market value as of the last revaluation date and assesses it at the state-mandated 70 percent ratio. It also processes exemption applications and answers questions about how an assessment was set.

Programs listed on the city's page include the following.

  • Veterans exemption, which requires a recorded DD214 and at least 90 days of wartime service; record it before October 1 to receive it on the next bill
  • Disabled veterans exemption, with a Benefits Payment Statement due before October 1
  • Additional low income veterans exemption, applied for between February 1 and October 1 and renewed every two years
  • Elderly and totally disabled homeowners program, with applications accepted from February 1 to May 15
  • Blind and 100 percent disability exemptions

The office is on the courtyard level of 235 Grand Street. The main number is (203) 574-6821, and the exemption and renters' rebate line is (203) 574-6827.

Owners of rented property, other than residential property of up to six units where the owner lives, must return the annual income and expense report before June 1 or face a 10 percent penalty on the assessment.

sections.h2: When are Waterbury property taxes due, and what are the penalties?
sections.html:
Real estate tax is due in two halves, July 1 and January 1. The city mails bills in late June and the Tax Collector says no separate bill is sent for the second installment.

Payment must be made within a month of the due date. After that, interest is charged at 1.5 percent a month, which is 18 percent a year, running from the due date, with a minimum charge of $2.00 per bill. The city adds that failing to receive a bill does not cancel the tax or the interest, citing Connecticut General Statutes 12-130 and 12-146.

sections.h2: What does the state conveyance tax mean for a Waterbury seller?
sections.html:
A seller of Waterbury real estate files the Connecticut conveyance tax return when the deed is recorded. The Department of Revenue Services requires Form OP-236 for any price of $2,000 or more, and Waterbury's town code on the form is 151.

If the property is a principal residence and the price will not cover the mortgages and priority taxes and liens, the state exemption for that situation may apply. The same exemption list includes a principal residence conveyed in lieu of foreclosure. Both can matter to an owner who owes more than a sale will bring.

Ask your attorney or the town clerk about the municipal share, because some state exemptions do not remove it.

sections.h2: Which employers and institutions shape Waterbury?
sections.html:
The City of Waterbury is the largest employer, with 4,081 people in the city's 2024 annual financial report, followed by two hospitals and a university.

The city also hosts regional campuses of UConn, the University of Bridgeport and Western Connecticut State University. Wikipedia notes that the city suffered an economic decline in the 1970s and 1980s.

sections.h2: How do people travel to and from Waterbury?
sections.html:
Interstate 84 and Route 8 meet downtown at the elevated William W. Deady Bridge, known locally as the MixMaster, which Wikipedia describes as one of the most congested interchanges in the New York and Connecticut region.

Metro-North's Waterbury Branch runs to Bridgeport with connections to Grand Central Terminal, and Waterbury is the end of that line. CT Transit buses leave from Exchange Place downtown, and a busway route links Waterbury with New Britain. The closest commercial airports are Bradley International and Tweed New Haven, and Waterbury-Oxford Airport serves general aviation.

Winters are cold and snowy. January's average high is 35 degrees and the low is 15, and annual precipitation runs about 53.6 inches, which is worth remembering when you assess an older roof or a chimney.

faqs.q: When are Waterbury real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due July 1 and the second half January 1. The city mails one bill in late June and sends no bill for the second installment.

faqs.q: What interest does Waterbury charge on late taxes?
faqs.a: Payment must be made within a month of the due date. After that, interest is 1.5 percent a month, or 18 percent a year, from the due date, with a $2.00 minimum per bill.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Waterbury assessment?
faqs.a: The Assessor's Office at (203) 574-6821, on the courtyard level of 235 Grand Street. The Tax Collector handles bills at (203) 574-6810.

faqs.q: Does Waterbury assess property at full value?
faqs.a: No. Property is appraised at market value as of the last revaluation date and assessed at the state-mandated 70 percent ratio.

faqs.q: What is Waterbury's town code on the conveyance tax form?
faqs.a: The Department of Revenue Services lists 151 for Waterbury on Form OP-236, which the seller files when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Waterbury house if I am behind on taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid tax and interest are paid from the proceeds at closing, using a written payoff from the Tax Collector.
